ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a gray rectangular region, with two identical white circles inside. The left circle is tangent to the top side, bottom side, and left side of the rectangle; the right circle is tangent to the top side, bottom side, and right side of the rectangle; the two circles are externally tangent at the middle position of the rectangle. Reasoning: The problem gives that the radius of each circle is 1. Because each circle is tangent to both the top and bottom sides of the rectangle, the height of the rectangle equals the diameter of the circle, namely 2. The two circles are externally tangent, so the distance between the two centers is 1+1=2. The distance from the center of the left circle to the left side is 1, and the distance from the center of the right circle to the right side is 1, therefore the width of the rectangle is 1+2+1=4. The area of the rectangle is 4×2=8. The total area of the two circles is 2·π·1^2=2π. The shaded area equals the area of the rectangle minus the areas of the two circles, namely 8-2π.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a rectangle shaded gray with two unshaded congruent circles inside it. The left circle is tangent to the top, bottom, and left sides of the rectangle; the right circle is tangent to the top, bottom, and right sides; the two circles touch externally at the center. From the text, each radius is 1. Since each circle touches the top and bottom sides, the rectangle height is one diameter, 2. The centers are 2 units apart because the circles are externally tangent, and each center is 1 unit from its adjacent vertical side, so the rectangle width is 1+2+1=4. Compute shaded area as rectangle area minus the two circle areas: 4·2 - 2π(1)^2 = 8 - 2π.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as two identical side-by-side configurations inside the same rectangle: the left circle fills the height and touches the left side, while the right circle fills the height and touches the right side, and they meet at a central tangent point. From the text, radius is 1, so each circle has diameter 2. Imagine drawing a vertical line through the point where the two circles touch; this divides the rectangle into two congruent 2-by-2 squares, each containing one circle tangent to three sides and to the dividing line at one point. The shaded area in one half is the square area minus the circle area, 2·2 - π(1)^2 = 4 - π. Double this for the two halves: 2(4 - π) = 8 - 2π.
